queries.query: Saturn speaking in his own voice, complaining that his six brothers cast him out to be their examiner and clothed him in a perishable body, though gold and silver come out purified from his water
queries.note: Saturn's speech in the canons; 'thrust me forth from a spiritual place', 'penetrate my body and perish in the fire' paraphrased; Saturn and the six brothers kept as the conceit any reader of the canons knows.

queries.note: The Seven Canons and the transposition of metals; 'Sol and Luna', 'brilliant and altogether royal metal', 'clear in its esse' paraphrased into silver/gold; the seven rules kept as the book's own announced frame.
